newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Abidjan bourse ends down in holiday-dampened trade.
newsitem.headline: Abidjan bourse ends down in holiday-dampened trade.

text.p: The Abidjan bourse ended lower this week, and, while volume was up on last week, trading was dull because many players are away on holiday.
Thursday saw a joint share and bond session because Friday, when bonds are normally traded, is a public holiday in Ivory Coast.
The BVA all-share index ended 3.14 percent lower than last Friday at 455.09, but is still 27.19 percent up on the year to date.
Bank BICICI was the most active stock for the second week running, accounting for almost a third of the total 156.5 million CFA francs ($250,000) of shares traded.
Dealers were unable to explain the interest. The shares were unchanged in price from last week at 46,000 CFA francs.
Edible oils producer Trituraf, which made its market debut this month, forged ahead, adding 700 to 7,580. It was floated at 6,250 CFA francs.
Among the fallers, Shell-CI lost 710 CFA francs to 13,550 and utilities company SODECI 690 to 20,000 ($ = 620 CFA francs) -- Abidjan newsroom, +225 21 90 90
